name: Petrov Homogeneous Vacuum
description: An empty spacetime that is curved and still the same at every event: four symmetries carry any event to any other in exactly one way, and no other vacuum without a cosmological constant has such a group. Its light cones turn steadily as one walks along one direction, and it is the field outside a cylinder of dust that spins with the circle round its surface a path of light.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Aleksei Petrov is remembered for sorting gravitational fields by the algebra of their curvature, and at Kazan State University he went on to sort them a second way, by their symmetries [petrov1954, petrov1962]. A motion, in his language, is a shift of a spacetime that leaves every distance in it alone, and the motions of a spacetime form a group [petrov1962]. He listed seven line elements in 1962, each with its group [petrov1962]. For the first six the group is intransitive: it slides each event along a surface of three dimensions and cannot move it off [petrov1962]. The seventh has a group that carries any event to any other, in exactly one way, which is called simply transitive [petrov1962, gibbons2008petrov].¶So the seventh spacetime is empty and curved, and it is the same at every event [gibbons2008petrov]. How can curved emptiness have no special place? Gary Gibbons and Steffen Gielen describe it as a hyperbolic plane with a flat plane of one time and one space direction standing over each of its points [gibbons2008petrov]. Walk across the hyperbolic plane in the direction $r$ and the flat plane over your head turns, light cones and all, through the same angle for every step [gibbons2008petrov]. After $2\pi\ell/\sqrt{3}$, about 3.6 times the one length $\ell$ of the solution, the cones stand upside down, and a clock there runs backward in the coordinate $t$ it started with [gibbons2008petrov].¶Without a cosmological constant it is the only empty spacetime of its kind, which Hans Stephani and his coauthors give as a theorem: the only vacuum solution whose whole group of motions is a simply transitive group of four is Petrov's [stephani2003, gibbons2008petrov]. A negative cosmological constant allows one counterpart, found in the same year by Vladimir Kaigorodov, also of Kazan, and a positive one allows none [kaigorodov1962, gibbons2008petrov]. Since every event is reached exactly once, the spacetime is a copy of its own group: choose an origin, and each event is the motion that carries the origin there [gibbons2008petrov]. Joan Josep Ferrando and Juan Antonio Sáez found a test for it that needs no coordinates, which is that a vacuum whose curvature has three different eigenvalues, each the same at every event, is Petrov's [ferrando2006].¶What could make such a field? An infinitely long cylinder of dust in rigid rotation can, the one Kornel Lanczos and Willem Jacob van Stockum had each solved by 1937 [lanczos1924, vanstockum1937]. William Bonnor recognised Petrov's spacetime in the vacuum outside it, for the one cylinder whose dust turns so fast that the circle round its surface is a path of light [bonnor1979petrov, gibbons2008petrov]. The field of every such cylinder has three symmetries, and it gains the fourth at that spin alone, where the invariants of its curvature are the same at every radius [bonnor1980, gibbons2008petrov]. Rolled up round the cylinder, the turning cones are Frank Tipler's time machine, in which circles about the axis are closed timelike curves [tipler1974, gibbons2008petrov].¶Could anyone build it? Gibbons and Gielen tried, on paper, to spin a slower cylinder up by throwing particles onto it [gibbons2008petrov]. Closed timelike curves first appear at half of Petrov's spin, and they found that a particle carrying enough angular momentum to push the cylinder past that mark is turned back before it reaches the dust [gibbons2008petrov]. They set the result beside Stephen Hawking's chronology protection conjecture, the proposal that the laws of physics forbid closed timelike curves from appearing [hawking1992, gibbons2008petrov]. Left unrolled, with every coordinate running over the whole real line, the spacetime is geodesically complete: every freely falling particle and every ray of light runs on forever [gibbons2008petrov].¶The four motions hold two smaller groups of three, of Bianchi's types I and VII, the types that sort the homogeneous cosmologies, and here each acts on surfaces that hold a time direction [gibbons2008petrov, terzis2009]. The metric came back in 2009, when Petros Terzis and T. Christodoulakis wrote down the general vacuum solution of type VII and found Petrov's inside it [terzis2009]. Among Thomas Lewis's rotating cylinders it is the one whose Kretschmann scalar, the usual gauge of how curved a vacuum is, vanishes at every event [lewis1932, costa2021]. Gibbons and Gielen deformed its group and found Kaigorodov's among the neighbours, with anti-de Sitter space's beside it [gibbons2008petrov].

related.text: Petrov's vacuum is one of Lewis's rotating cylinders, the member of the Lewis class at $m = \sqrt{3}$. At that value the field gains a fourth symmetry and becomes the same at every event [bonnor1979petrov, bonnor1980].

The cylinder of dust that Petrov's vacuum surrounds. William Bonnor showed in 1979 that the field outside it is Petrov's when the dust turns at the angular velocity $c/R$, with $R$ the radius of the cylinder [bonnor1979petrov].

Kaigorodov's spacetime, the simplest of Siklos's waves, is the counterpart with a negative cosmological constant: the other vacuum whose four symmetries reach every event exactly once. Gary Gibbons and Steffen Gielen found its group among the deformations of Petrov's [kaigorodov1962, gibbons2008petrov].
Another spacetime that is the same at every event and holds closed timelike curves. Gödel's is filled with rotating dust and Petrov's is empty [godel1949, gibbons2008petrov].

Kasner's universe is the same at every place, and Petrov's at every time as well. Joan Josep Ferrando and Juan Antonio Sáez found both in one family, the vacuums of Petrov's type I with a symmetry aligned to the curvature [ferrando2006].
Petrov's group holds groups of Bianchi's types I and VII. They act on surfaces with a time direction in them, and a Bianchi cosmology's group acts on space [gibbons2008petrov, terzis2009].

coordinates.name: Petrov

parameters.description: The one length of the solution, Petrov's $1/k$; the plane of $r$ and $z$ is a hyperbolic plane of curvature $-1/\ell^2$
Phase of the plane of $t$ and $\phi$, whose light cones turn through $\psi/2$; the coordinates $t$ and $\phi$ exchange the parts of time and space each time $\psi$ grows by $\pi$

coordinates.convention: We use Petrov's coordinates $(t, r, \phi, z)$ in the letters of Gibbons and Gielen, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$, $\phi$, and $z$ lengths, each running over the whole real line. The future is the side of $\cos(\psi/2)\,\partial_t + \sin(\psi/2)\,\partial_\phi$, which is timelike at every $r$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Dust Cylinder
domains: r = R \;\text{(the surface of the dust, where the circle of constant } t, r, z \text{ is null)}
L < 0 \;\text{(the circles of constant } t, r, z \text{ are closed timelike curves)}

parameters.description: Radius of the dust cylinder, a length; the vacuum is $r \ge R$, and the dust turns at the angular velocity $c/R$
Petrov's length, the scale of $r$ and $z$; the vacuum joins the dust on the surface where $\ell = R/\sqrt{e}$
Phase of van Stockum's functions, zero on the surface, and the phase of Petrov's chart
Minus the norm of $\partial_t$, equal to 1 on the surface and negative from $\psi = \pi/3$ to $\psi = 4\pi/3$
van Stockum's cross term, a length, equal to $R$ on the surface

The norm of $\partial_\phi$, so that $FL + M^2 = r^2$; it vanishes on the surface, and the circles of constant $t$, $r$, and $z$ are closed timelike curves where it is negative, out to $r = e^{\pi/\sqrt{3}}R$

coordinates.convention: We use van Stockum's coordinates $(t, r, \phi, z)$ outside his dust cylinder of radius $R$, which rotate with the dust at the angular velocity $c/R$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $r$ and $z$ lengths, and $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$. Petrov's radius is $\ell\ln(r/R)$, and his $t$ and $\phi$ are linear in these. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
